Under Article 25, the contract may impose a maximum notice period of no more than two months (point (d)). The transition must be completed within a mandatory maximum transitional period of 30 calendar days, initiated after the notice period, during which the provider must assist the customer and maintain business continuity (Article 25(2)(a)); if 30 days is technically unfeasible, the provider must justify this within 14 working days and may set an alternative period of up to seven months (Article 25(4)). As for charges: in March 2026 (i.e., between 11 January 2024 and 12 January 2027), the provider may impose only reduced switching charges under Article 29(2), which cannot exceed the costs directly linked to the switching process (Article 29(3)); from 12 January 2027 all switching charges are prohibited (Article 29(1)).

No, it cannot be registered. Under Article 18(c), an entity must operate on a not-for-profit basis and be legally independent from any entity that operates on a for-profit basis; legal control by a for-profit pharmaceutical group means it fails this requirement.

For a qualifying entity: under Article 19(5), once it has submitted all necessary information under paragraph 4 and the competent authority has evaluated the application and found it complies with Article 18, the authority must register it in the public national register within 12 weeks after receipt of the application. That registration is valid in all Member States, and the competent authority must notify the Commission, which includes it in the public Union register.

Data Governance Act - definition of 'data holder': a legal person, including public sector bodies and international organisations, or a natural person who is not a data subject with respect to the specific data in question, which, in accordance with applicable Union or national law, has the right to grant access to or to share certain personal data or non-personal data.
Data Act - definition of 'data holder': a natural or legal person that has the right or obligation, in accordance with this Regulation, applicable Union law or national legislation adopted in accordance with Union law, to use and make available data, including, where contractually agreed, product data or related service data which it has retrieved or generated during the provision of a related service.

Both definitions allow a natural person to be a data holder, but the Data Governance Act restricts this to a natural person who is not a data subject with respect to the specific data in question, whereas the Data Act allows any natural or legal person without that restriction. The status is based in both on having rights under applicable Union or national law, but the Data Governance Act focuses on the right to grant access to or to share personal or non-personal data, while the Data Act focuses on the right or obligation to use and make available data, including product data or related service data retrieved or generated during the provision of a related service.
